english: Let $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ be an arithmetic progression. The arithmetic mean of the ten observations $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{10}$ is $23$, and the arithmetic mean of the twenty observations $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{20}$ is $43$. hindi: माना $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$ एक समान्तर श्रेढ़ी है। दस प्रेक्षणों $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{10}$ का समान्तर माध्य $23$ है तथा बीस प्रेक्षणों $a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_{20}$ का समान्तर माध्य $43$ है। तब बीस प्रेक्षणों $a_{11},a_{12},\ldots,a_{30}$ का समान्तर माध्य है
solution: Mean of $n$ consecutive AP terms $=$ average of first and last: mean of $a_1,\ldots,a_n=a+\dfrac{(n-1)d}{2}$
solution_full: Let the first term be $a$ and the common difference $d$.
The sum of the first $n$ terms is $S_n=\dfrac n2\left(2a+(n-1)d\right)$, so the mean of $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ is $\dfrac{S_n}{n}=a+\dfrac{(n-1)d}{2}$.
$a_{11}=5+40=45$ and $a_{30}=5+116=121$. The mean of the consecutive terms $a_{11},\ldots,a_{30}$ is the mean of the first and last of them: $\dfrac{45+121}{2}=83$.
originality_note: New: two running means of an AP fix the progression, and the mean of a block that overlaps the known data only in part is asked (way 5: AP sums and the arithmetic mean). Closest known: 'the mean of the first n terms of an AP'. Different because: the block a11..a30 extends beyond the data given, so the student must recover a and d first.
stem_review: Read as a student: every observation, class, symbol and condition is introduced before use, the class-boundary convention is explicit where it matters, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions / sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Changed: No change.
key_step: Writing each mean as a + (n-1)d/2, solving for a and d, and averaging the end terms of the new block.
justification: A routine chain of AP sum formulae with one trap (the block mean 63 versus 83). Comparable to the routine statistics recovery of 2026-P2-Q12 (L2).

concept_use.Arithmetic mean of ungrouped data: Mean = sum / number of observations for the blocks a1..a10, a1..a20 and a11..a30.
concept_use.Arithmetic Progression (AP) & Sum of AP: S_n = n/2 (2a + (n-1)d) gives the two equations and the mean of the block.
